text:
Anya K.: quick design/copy review — we're updating the "Revoke API key" confirmation. want to settle on tone, exact button copy, and a11y notes. current modal below + three options.

Anya K.: Current (in staging):
```
Title: Revoke API key
Body: Are you sure you want to revoke this API key? Applications using it will stop working.
Primary: Revoke
Secondary: Cancel
```

Matt R.: main question: do we give the user a hint about rotating keys vs revoking? sometimes products offer 'rotate' which revokes + issues new key.

Anya K.: good point. backend doesn't auto-issue a replacement. we could add a link to docs about rotation.

Kevin L.: copy should explicitly say where the key is used (if we can surface that). else people might accidentally break infra.

Lucy P.: accessibility: mention model name in aria-label, and we should avoid ambiguous single-word buttons like "Revoke" for screen readers. also ensure dialog is announced with role=alertdialog and keyboard traps focus.

Anya K.: draft variants: 
```
Option 1 — explicit consequences:
Title: Revoke API key
Body: Revoking this key will immediately stop any applications that use it. This cannot be undone. Check usage in the API keys page before revoking.
Primary: Revoke API key
Secondary: Keep key

Option 2 — recovery-forward:
Title: Revoke API key
Body: This will deactivate the key. If you need a replacement, create a new key on the API keys page. Existing integrations will stop working right away.
Primary: Revoke and close
Secondary: Cancel

Option 3 — short + help link:
Title: Revoke key?
Body: Deactivates the key immediately.
Small link: Learn about key rotation
Primary: Revoke
Secondary: Cancel
```

Matt R.: I like Option 1 but tweak the CTA to include "immediately" — legal/ops teams like explicit timing.

Kevin L.: prefer "Revoke API key" (full phrase) as primary. Avoid jargon like "Deactivate" in the button. And yes to the docs link.

Lucy P.: suggested ARIA examples: primary button aria-label="Revoke API key MyAppKey-2026" and dialog role="alertdialog" aria-labelledby linking to the title. Also add visually-hidden text: "This action cannot be undone." so screen readers encounter the legal bit before the CTA.

DesignBot: copy style recommendation: use sentence case for body, title case for primary action is fine. Proposed final: 
```
Title: Revoke API key
Body: Revoking this key will immediately stop any applications that use it. This action cannot be undone.
Small link: Learn about key rotation (opens in a new tab)
Primary: Revoke API key
Secondary: Cancel
ARIA notes: <div role="alertdialog" aria-labelledby="revoke-title">; <button aria-label="Revoke API key MyAppKey-2026">Revoke API key</button>; visually-hidden span: "This action cannot be undone."
```

Anya K.: nice. one more product nit: if we can show a count of recent uses (e.g., "Used 3 times in the past 7 days") on the modal, that'll help people decide. can we add that?

Kevin L.: backend can surface last-used timestamp and usage count. agree it's helpful. keep it small, under the body.

Lucy P.: also add focus order: title -> body -> usage hint -> primary -> secondary. ESC closes dialog and returns focus to the API key row. Ensure focus ring contrast on primary CTA.

Matt R.: should we require typing the key name for org owners? maybe a configurable step for enterprise. default flow stays single confirm.

Anya K.: agreed — I'll add a note to the enterprise docs and add an optional "Require confirmation text" toggle for org settings. For this modal, I'll go with the DesignBot copy + usage hint + docs link.

DesignBot: saved copy to /docs/ui-copy/api-keys/revoke-modal and flagged for engineering with aria snippets.
